verdict.label: contradictory
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report an unadjusted correlation between circulating adiponectin and LDL cholesterol in comparable metabolic-disease populations, but with opposite directions: study A (173 patients with type-2 DM) reports a positive correlation (r = 0.30, P = 0.001), while study B (180 individuals including MetS patients and controls) reports adiponectin levels negatively associated with LDL. The exposure (serum/plasma adiponectin), outcome (LDL), and association contrast are sufficiently similar, and neither abstract provides a text-supported contextual difference explaining the opposite directions.

source_evidence.quote: Adiponectin was negatively correlated with waist circumference (r = -0.16, P = 0.06) and positively with HbA1c (r = 0.19, P = 0.032), total cholesterol (r = 0.23, P = 0.017), LDL (r = 0.30, P = 0.001), SD-LDL (r = 0.41, P < 0.001), and SD-LDL/LDL (r = 0.22, P = 0.023).
Adiponectin levels were negatively associated with waist circumference, waist-hip ratio, PTX-3 and LDL.

diagnostics.notes: Extraction verified: side A correctly extracts the positive LDL correlation (r = 0.30, P = 0.001) from sentence 9; side B correctly extracts the negative LDL association from sentence 5. Both are directional association claims with the same exposure (adiponectin) and outcome (LDL). Populations differ (type-2 DM vs MetS/controls) but remain comparable metabolic-disease cohorts; no explicit explanatory difference is stated in either abstract.
